                 VI. T HREATS T O VALIDITY                                Because of the fragmentation of the Android ecosystem, An-
                                                                       droid apps can exhibit inconsistencies in their behavior when
   As it is the case for most empirical evaluation, there are
                                                                       they are run on different platforms. To help developers identify
both construct and external threats to validity associated with
                                                                       these behavioral inconsistencies before developers release their
our results. In terms of construct validity, there might be errors
                                                                       apps, we propose a technique called D IFF D ROID. D IFF D ROID
in the implementation of our technique. To mitigate this threat,
                                                                       aims to identify and suitably report behavioral inconsistencies
we extensively inspected the results of the evaluation manually.
                                                                       in Android apps by combining input generation, behavior
In terms of external validity, our results might not generalize
                                                                       modeling, and differential testing.
to other apps or CPIs. In particular, we only considered a
                                                                          We implemented and empirically evaluated D IFF D ROID by
limited number of apps. This limitation is an artifact of the
                                                                       running it on 5 real-world benchmark apps and over 130
complexity involved in manually inspecting results deriving
                                                                       different platforms. Our results provide initial evidence that
from executions on a large set of devices (over 130). To
                                                                       D IFF D ROID can identify CPIs on real apps efficiently and with
mitigate this threat, we used randomly selected real-world apps
                                                                       a limited number of false positives.
from different domains.
                                                                          In future work, we will first extend our evaluation by con-

generated by such fragmentation. Their work systematically             that it handles inconsistencies other than visual ones (e.g.,

and proposes a method for tracking fragmentation. In this              processed). Fourth, we will investigate whether precision and

challenges involved in developing apps due to the differences          class classifier approach. Fifth, we will investigate techniques
in size and display resolution of different devices. Our work          for suggesting repairs for the CPIs identified by D IFF D ROID.
helps developers in this challenging task by automatically             Finally, and more on the engineering side, we will investigate

   The work on Android fragmentation led to studies on
